Job Description

The Advance Computing Solutions group in the NLR Computational Science Center has an opening for a graduate intern in computational synthesis, with a particular emphasis on development and utilization of an agentic AI framework that automates the exploration of relevant reaction energetics using machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). The researcher will work with an interdisciplinary team to develop agentic AI that automates the training of MLIPs of desirable accuracy and uses the trained MLIPs to discern the effect of varying different reaction conditions on the final synthesized Fe-N-C fuel cel catalyst.

We are looking for a dynamic, motivated researcher with a strong technical background and an interest in the mission of NLR. The successful candidate will collaborate with NLR staff and researchers to develop agentic AI for the optimization of Fe-N-C catalyst synthesis.

- Development of agentic AI framework that automates the training of MLIPs and the exploration of the combinatorial space of reactions relevant to Fe-N-C catalyst synthesis and their energetics
- Collaboration with NLR researchers to use the developed AI to study the chemistry of graphitization and Fe incorporation into the N-C matrix for different synthetic precursors, e.g. iron salts and zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) linkers.
- Development of AI that processes, analyzes, and visualizes results from simulations provide chemical insight and intuition into important chemical reactions.
- Authoring, presenting and assisting in the preparation of technical papers, reports and conference proceedings on topics related to AI-automated MLIP studies of the synthesis of Fe-N-C fuel cell catalysts.

What We Do

The SEI helps advance software engineering principles and practices and serves as a national resource in software engineering, computer security, and process improvement. The SEI works closely with defense and government organizations, industry, and academia to continually improve software-intensive systems. Our core purpose is to help organizations improve software engineering capabilities and develop or acquire the right software, defect free, within budget and on time, every time.

Position Summary

As an AI Engineer Intern within the SEI AI Division’s Mission Innovation Lab, you will help take applied AI research ideas from concept to prototype in support of defense and national security missions. You will work alongside senior researchers and machine learning engineers to explore and apply large-scale foundation models (such as GPT and LLaMA), agentic AI workflows, and traditional machine learning techniques to real-world mission use cases. During your internship, you will assist in designing experimental prototypes, building data and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, and running evaluations to help translate emerging AI advancements into secure, reliable, and scalable mission capabilities.

Requirements

· Enrolled in a degree granting program (Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field).

· Willingness to travel to various locations to support the SEI’s overall mission. This includes within the SEI and CMU community.

· You will be subject to a background check and must be eligible to work in the United States without Visa sponsorship.

Duties

· Assist in designing and prototyping autonomous agents and multi-step pipelines using frameworks such as LangChain, ReAct, tool-calling, or the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

· Build and maintain data pipelines, ETL processes, and backend services using Python, C/C++, or Java.

· Contribute to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that integrate external knowledge bases with Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve factual accuracy.

· Support rapid prototyping, benchmarking, and robustness or adversarial testing of AI models in realistic environments.

· Research and stay current with emerging LLM architectures, agentic paradigms, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA) methods, and AI-safety techniques.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

· Proficiency in Python and familiarity with at least one compiled language (such as C/C++ or Java), REST/GraphQL APIs, or containerization.

· Foundational understanding of machine learning theory (supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning) and standard evaluation metrics.

· Academic or practical experience working with deep learning frameworks (such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX) and LLM libraries (such as Hugging Face Transformers or LangChain).

· Analytical thinking with the ability to decompose complex AI problems into tractable components and iterate rapidly.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills for documenting designs and presenting results to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

· Proven teamwork, high curiosity, and autonomy to collaborate in interdisciplinary groups, contribute to shared codebases, and explore emerging technologies.

Desired Experience

· Experience fine-tuning LLMs or building multi-tool agents, planner-executor loops, or tool-calling pipelines through coursework, research, or personal projects.

· Exposure to deploying ML/LLM APIs (e.g., FastAPI, gRPC) or working with data-pipeline tools (e.g., Airflow, Prefect, Ray).

· Familiarity with building evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, or data quality pipelines for machine learning or agentic systems.

· Contributions to open-source AI/ML libraries, agentic frameworks, or prior research experience relevant to defense or government AI applications.

Job Function Breakdown

50% AI Prototyping & Software Engineering: Assisting in the design, coding, and deployment of agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and backend services in Python, C/C++, or Java.

30% Applied Research, Benchmarking & Testing: Conducting literature reviews on emerging LLM/agentic paradigms, running benchmarks, and assisting with robustness and adversarial evaluations.

10% Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Documenting experimental designs, codebases, and evaluation results, and presenting findings to team members and stakeholders.

10% Team Collaboration & Mentorship: Collaborating with senior researchers and engineers to refine problem statements, participating in code reviews, and engaging in SEI learning opportunities.

TOTAL = 100%
